title: d-12: beads-cache-and-release
description:
## Deliverables
1. Migrate actual beads-cache@8e883ee CacheScheduleStore and scheduler calls to published sc-storage/sc-runtime-db-sqlite/sc-cron0.3.0. Deliver the upstream migration PR and validate app+cron writes through its shared writer, preserving existing data and cron behavior — REQ-RUN-0002; REQ-CRON-0004; ADR-RUN-0020.
2. Own registry runner/workflow, archive rehearsal and actual eight-crate coordinated0.3.0 publication in dependency order with sc-storage first. Run fresh registry-only upstream/cron, server/rmcp and test-util helper consumers with the release-tested dependency combination, with advisory/source/native-identity checks — REQ-RUN-0002/0702; NFR-RUN-0007; ANC-012.
3. Update root README, release notes/project status and applicable controlled-host benchmark evidence to the actual published surface. Preserve kit/recovery rules and do not claim a source checkout or copied facade is the upstream migration — REQ-RUN-0702; NFR-RT-0001.

4. Remove tests/integration/cron-consumer/schema/Cargo.toml rmcp =3.8.0 pin in this sole-owned consumer manifest: use >=3.9 because3.9.x is the tested patched minimum for RUSTSEC-2026-0462 under the ADR-RUN-0203 amendment. Raising the floor removes older vulnerable releases; every later release from3.9 is admitted with no upper bound. Preserve the existing server/default-features selection and run the normal registry consumer tests and apply req:REQ-RUN-0002/package-caps (ADR-RUN-0203; ANC-037). Also convert tests/integration/cron-consumer/Cargo.toml Windows dev-dependencies to win32job >=2.0.3 and waitpid-any >=0.3.0, preserving purpose comments and running the normal Windows tests. d-3/d-5/d-9 retain their own pin-line edits; this sprint does not repeat them.

5. Reuse d-3's check_dependency_manifests(paths) on exact unpacked archives and generated-template defaults; wire it into archive rehearsal, registry consumer validation and upload. Own only input assembly and release fixtures. SDK registry requirements use >= floors with no upper bound; consumer pins are allowed (ANC-037). Remove the interim rule after equivalent sc-lint#936 release and adoption, as recorded by ADR-RUN-0005.

6. Own final recommendation generation after0.3.0 conversion and registry availability: template/scripts/tested_dependencies.py, template/cargo-generate.toml and template/.sc-runtime/** deliver the newest tested Cargo.lock and matching .sc-runtime/tested-dependencies.json for each supported profile (ANC-038). The script runs after normal project-name prefixing. Verify every recorded name/version/source matches the lock and real --locked build/tests; consumer pins remain free.

## This sprint does not close
Generated app composition/transports are d-11-owned. This sprint prepares alongside d-11, consumes d-3's checker, and merges completed d-11 before archive rehearsal/upload. No duplicate template wiring, template-only registry subject or second checker.
Apply template/cargo-generate.toml changes only after the completed d-11 merge: preserve its existing layout/cron choices and validation hook, remove Cargo.lock suppression as needed for recommendation delivery and add the recommendation script after project-name prefixing. No concurrent section ownership.
design:
## Exact released-consumer subject
beads-cache source8e883ee99cb9c34dfb89fb39e25323d54ae6f2ad uses path sc-cron and already stores schedules in its app DB through CacheScheduleStore (`crates/bd-cache-store/src/schedule.rs:80,164`). Record the source and intentional API changes in tests/registry/phase-d/beads-cache/README.md. Migrate that adapter and actual scheduler calls to sc-cron CronStore over Storage<CronRow> backed by the published generic sc-runtime-db-sqlite shared channel writer. Retain existing application/schedule rows, stable identifiers, generation fencing, row limits and atomic multi-row transitions. No local path/patch/Git SDK dependency can satisfy final acceptance. A recorded source reduction is not falsely described as an upstream beads-cache PR having landed; if the actual migration needs an upstream PR, coordinate it with its owner and retain the outcome as a release predicate.
The release-test lock selects the adopted exact release identities for sc-storage, sc-runtime-db-sqlite, sc-cron and applicable runtime/command packages from crates.io. The exact selection is a release-test identity, not a restrictive production third-party range. Direct rusqlite uses the owner-directed >=0.41 requirement with no upper bound and required bundled/hooks/functions/trace features; d-12 releases that d-6-qualified uncapped range, without a capped qualification fallback. Verify one libsqlite3-sys>=0.39; run normal tests with the selected versions. No SQLx SQLite driver remains in the generated SQLite consumer. SQLx PostgreSQL/MySQL-only graphs must not gain a SQLite native edge; a selected SQLite feature would change that exposure and is not inferred absent from a crate name.

## Registry runner/workflow interface
Own `.github/workflows/phase-d-registry.yml` and `tests/registry/phase-d/run.py` together. The workflow invokes `python3 tests/registry/phase-d/run.py --version <adopted-version> --source crates-io`; the version has one adopted source. It checks the migrated beads-cache subject, server/rmcp and test-util helper subjects, plus the actual migrated beads-cache SQLite+cron application. Isolate registry consumer locks, assert sources/versions using Cargo metadata, execute actual builds/tests and `cargo deny check advisories` without ignoring RUSTSEC-2026-0459/0462. The positive result requires all assertions/audits/tests; missing release/consumer, wrong source/native identity or failed command exits nonzero. Controlled failure inputs prove fail-closed paths; only the actual post-publication run is registry proof. Ordinary inherited source CI is insufficient.
Consumer: release reviewer/maintainers; capability: eight-package published channel writer + shared app storage; observed defect: consumers blocked by native-link/advisory constraints and separate cron topology; delete the dedicated workflow when the standard kit post-publish hook performs the same consumer checks.

## Rehearsal and failure handling
Use the configured kit to package all8 crates. Inspect actual Cargo.toml.orig/normalized manifest, README, features and source comments explaining each extra cap. Unpack exactly these .crate archives into a temporary rehearsal workspace with rehearsal-only patches to their extracted contents; build/test the same consumers before upload. Record hashes; upload those exact archives. This is archive rehearsal, not registry proof. Discard every patch/source replacement and start final proof from fresh registry resolution after publication.
Publish sc-storage first; derive the remaining topological order from final manifests. Existing sc-config/sc-transport and sc-command precede their actual consumers; writer and cron follow sc-storage; sc-runtime and sc-cron-commands follow their applicable prerequisites. All8 adopted versions must be present. Do not invent a fixed order that contradicts actual dependencies.
On mid-sequence transport/index failure, stop, query exact published versions/hashes and retry only missing uploads of identical approved archives. Never republish an occupied version. For a real package/consumer/security defect, stop remaining uploads; release owner yanks newly published defective packages/dependent siblings if leaving them selectable would break consumers or retain a target advisory. Do not yank for transient network/CI errors or unrelated audit findings. An occupied defective version requires source-owner fixes plus a coordinated replacement patch of the adopted train, repeated rehearsal and fresh registry proof; issues remain open on partial/failed publication.

## Required validation and limits
Run `just lint`, `just test`, workspace build, actual `sc-lint lint sc-boundary --root . --config sc-lint.toml`, normal root/separate-consumer tests (generated proof belongs to d-11) and selected Windows/Monty tests. Install all prerequisites; a documented command is not a pass. Use `python3 scripts/benchmark/check_release_evidence.py`; the newest applicable `site/reports/benchmark-monty/*.campaign.json` + HTML twin must match the source-equivalence contract, otherwise refresh on the existing controlled host procedure. No timing/sleep-based correctness tests. Generated daemon/CLI/schema/wizard wiring is owned by d-11; this dependent sprint proves the upstream application. No synchronization/code generator/config-reload/unspecified permissions work.

Release version is approved coordinated0.3.0 for all8 crates; per-crate rationale is authoritative in run-phase-d design. ScheduleStore/SqliteScheduleStore are removed in the coordinated breaking0.3.0 release; no0.2.x release carries that removal.


## Independent integration artifacts
Consumes d-3 qualified dependency/API and normal tests, d-4 CLI/action used by publishing-kit tooling, d-5 manifests/contracts/eight-package targets, d-6 generic writer/atomic backend; d-9 CronStore/row migration and d-9 awaited scheduler/command adapter. It consumes d-10 public sc-command combinators and the d-3 manifest-check callable; it does not duplicate d-11 generated daemon wiring or d-7/8 stores. Its registry subjects are actual upstream beads-cache/cron-consumer, server/rmcp and helper. D-12 prepares in the third wave alongside d-11 and checks completed generated integration before upload.
Actual beads-cache app and schedule mutations share one writer/file; it has no SQLx SQLite driver, no ATM/sc-compose production dependency and no caller blocking or spawn_blocking. Only dedicated writer runtime uses block_on; reader threads use blocking_recv and no runtime. Dependency declarations follow req:REQ-RUN-0002/package-caps. Exact SDK0.3.0 release identities are evidence subjects, not third-party production restrictions.
## Internal release order and exact external closure
Prepare runner fault cases and migrate beads-cache in parallel with d-11. Before archive rehearsal/upload, bd show run-d-11.group-sanity --json must show status=closed with the actual generated integration validation; upload also waits for package-caps to pass on the exact archives. D-11 completion is a required pre-upload predicate; it does not block independent preparation. Also require randlee ratification for pending ADR/template extension and the actual passing safety checks required by the owner sprints; absence keeps publication open, never fake a pass.
After the gate: regenerate canonical Cargo.lock and apply coordinated0.3.0 version bump plus sibling version-to-workspace inheritance in root and owned public manifests/template workspace inputs. In the one exact post-conversion archive rehearsal, validate the actual beads-cache migration against the unpacked archives before the first upload, then publish those exact archives. Discard archive rehearsal patches and run fresh registry-only consumer proofs after upload. Source fixtures are not published proof.
External work owner: beads-cache maintainer (user/randlee), with sprint developer preparing the migration PR. Sprint closure requires upstream PR OPEN and CI GREEN at a recorded SHA against published0.3.0 SDK crates; record URL/SHA and actual source assertions in tests/registry/phase-d/beads-cache/README.md. Merge is not required for sprint/phase closure. If maintainer does not respond, keep d-12/open external follow-up; a fork/draft/source copy is not success. No unauthorized upstream merge. Existing downstream app tests establish its preserved behavior; do not duplicate d-11 generated-app criteria here.
Single canonical root Cargo.lock owner is d-12. Earlier source owners regenerate disposable worktree locks to satisfy each closure tests; they do not commit lock updates. D-12 normalizes one final lock after d-3/d-5/d-6/d-9/d-10 close. Selected native-library proof is cargo tree, never lockfile entries. d-12 takes shared manifest version registration after those named dependency handoffs, leaving0.2.0 development baseline unpublishable until final conversion. Package sc-command exports/README must match d-10 actual helpers.
Root-manifest counterpart: d-12 edits only sc-* release version lines after the d-6 handoff; it never edits the workspace rusqlite line, whose qualified shared range is d-6-owned.
Single-checker ownership: d-3 owns tests/unit/generation/test_runtime_ecosystem_upgrade.py and check_dependency_manifests(paths). d-12 supplies exact archive inputs and upload integration only; no duplicate policy fixtures or checker tests. D-12 owns final generated recommendation production. Its development prerequisites are d-3/d-4/d-6/d-9/d-10; d-11 completion is the checked pre-upload merge/publication predicate, not a development blocker.

req:REQ-RUN-0002/release — Rehearse exact8crate archives before publication; package manifests/READMEs/features/comments match actual APIs and approved0.3.0. Wrong or missing release/source, advisory/native mismatch or failed command exits nonzero. Controlled negatives test refusal; only actual post-publication consumer builds/tests prove delivery. Apply package-caps to the exact unpacked SDK manifests, not consumer-owned pins.
Required commands: just lint; just test; cargo build --workspace; sc-lint lint sc-boundary --root . --config sc-lint.toml; kit package/rehearsal and fresh registry runner the registry consumers; cargo deny check advisories for every registry subject; python3 scripts/benchmark/check_release_evidence.py with controlled-host evidence matching source-equivalence policy. Root README/release notes match package contents. d-11 generated integration is separately required for phase acceptance.
req:REQ-RUN-0002/publication-gate — Prepare migration/runner/recommendation generation in parallel with d-11. Before archive rehearsal/upload, merge completed d-11 generated composition and require its sanity closed, owner ratification and both actual external safety rules passing. Then final0.3.0 conversion, one exact eight-archive rehearsal, d-3 checker passing on those archives and fresh registry-only consumer proof. Missing predicates block publication, not independent development readiness. Immediately before the first upload, recheck the same publication predicate against the current source, completed d-11, ratification, safety-rule results and exact rehearsed archives.
req:REQ-RUN-0002/upstream-subject — Exact close predicate: upstream beads-cache PR open with CI green at recorded SHA using published0.3.0 SDKs, URL/SHA in owned consumer README. Maintainer=user/randlee; merge not required. No response or CI failure leaves sprint open with explicit external follow-up. No local path/patch/Git SDK substitute. sc-command package exports/docs match closed d-10; cargo tree checks selected native graph, not lockfile.
All changed public storage functions are typed Result/no-panic. Actual writer-panic callers receive typed errors; required no-panic/transaction analyzer evidence is not replaced by promises or a superficial grep. cargo build --workspace passes against the final coordinated train at this closure.
req:REQ-RUN-0002/package-caps — Call d-3's single manifest check on exact unpacked SDK manifests and generated-template defaults: registry requirements must use >= tested floors with no upper bound (ANC-037). A violation fails rehearsal, registry consumer proof and upload. Consumer-owned pins are permitted and outside this default-policy check. d-12 owns input assembly/wiring; the checker stays d-3-owned and root rusqlite registration stays d-5-owned; d-12 changes only SDK release-version lines.
req:REQ-RUN-0002/preserved-cron — In the actual upstream migration, the default app and cron data use the same SQLite file; the existing consumer tests verify rejection of a second active schedule with the same name and of a new schedule row at the embedding app's configured limit. Reuse the delivered cron behavior and existing upstream cases; do not build a second policy implementation (ANC-021/030/031).
req:REQ-RUN-0002/release-recommendations — Release-generated applications ship the tested latest-allowed registry Cargo.lock and .sc-runtime/tested-dependencies.json from the same actual profile build/test run (ANC-038). Metadata enumerates every locked package name/version/source and release/toolchain/profile identity, matches Cargo.lock, and is readable for later revert/upgrade tooling. Consumers can keep, replace or update the recommended lock and pin their own requirements. D-12 owns recommendation production and its generation script; d-11 owns unrelated app composition hooks.

dependencies.title: Phase D: shared app storage, channel writer and published consumer migration
dependencies.description:
Phase D makes the SDK easy to adopt and lets consumers choose dependency upgrades. Product intent is PRD v2.0; the release is the owner-selected eight public crates at0.3.0. Generic backends contain no consumer table code. Sprint metadata.owned_paths is the authoritative full file fence; summaries below are navigation only.

| Sprint | Wave | Boundary | Consumed artifacts |
|---|---|---|---|
| d-3 | 1 | dependency/source compatibility | none; owns the one manifest checker |
| d-4 | 1 | generation tooling | none |
| d-5 | 1 | storage/atomic/row contract | none; owner ratification and Active ADR0020/0021 before consumers |
| d-6 | 2 | SQLite backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-7 | 2 | Postgres backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-8 | 2 | MySQL backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-9 | 2 | cron domain adapter | d-5 production contract and additive legacy build |
| d-10 | 2 | common commands/transforms | d-3 compiled command server/schema/error ABI, d-5 Storage/row contract |
| d-11 | 3 | generated composition | d-3 checker, d-4 tools, d-6/7/8/9/10 code |
| d-12 | 3 | registry migration/release/recommendations | d-3 source/checker, d-4 tools, d-6/9/10 code; d-11 completion checked before upload |

Ten sprints; critical path3, width6. No dependency exists solely because two sprints edit the same manifest. The release and generated-integration sprints prepare in parallel; upload waits for completed generated integration. No implementation dispatch before plan approval.
dependencies.design:
PRD v2.0 governs product scope. sc-storage is std-only; storage/atomic/row traits are the shared contract, with only transaction name/mode properties. SQLite uses one async queue and one writer thread exclusively owning its sole write-mode connection, queued writes commit together, and replies follow commit. Only the writer runtime uses Runtime::block_on. Readers use blocking_recv without a runtime; async callers never block or use spawn_blocking to submit writes. Consumer rows/schema/migrations stay above generic engines. sc-cron implements its policy once over generic atomic Storage<CronRow> and keeps raw backend mutation out of the CronStore public facade.

D-5 owns contract types, shared registry/boundary definitions, required REQ/ADR amendments and the minimal legacy compatibility build. Its layer-file handoffs are additive contract/legacy artifacts on existing dependencies, not simultaneous same-wave edits. d-9 owns the0.3.0 removal of ScheduleStore/SqliteScheduleStore and obsolete SQLite files after those artifacts compile. Root Cargo.toml passes directly from d-5 registrations to d-12 release-version conversion; d-6 reads it. d-3 owns the command manifest with its rmcp3.9 server/schema compatibility code; d-10 consumes that compiled artifact and later adds storage helpers. Specific crate facade boundaries pass from d-5 to their implementation owner on the existing must-follow edges.

D-5 owner ratification is pending and gates its closure; ADR0020/0021 must be Active before d-6..d-12 start. The actual no-panic rule sc-lint#931 and transaction-safe analyzer remain required for affected owner-sprint closure and are rechecked before publication. Lead owns the external analyzer request; missing delivery is a real blocker, not a waiver.

D-3 owns the sole interim SDK manifest checker; d-11 invokes it on generated outputs and d-12 on exact archives/upload. Remove it after equivalent sc-lint#936 release/adoption. Published/template registry requirements are open tested floors (ANC-037); normal tests check the selected versions, with no dedicated min/latest jobs. Consumers may pin what they want. D-12 alone produces the final newest-tested Cargo.lock recommendation and matching .sc-runtime/tested-dependencies.json (ANC-038).

Eight published packages at0.3.0: sc-storage, sc-runtime-db-sqlite, sc-config, sc-transport, sc-command, sc-runtime, sc-cron, sc-cron-commands. Postgres/MySQL generic engines remain generated this phase under that approved packaging scope; their implementation fixes need template updates/regeneration, explicitly recorded in ADR0020. They do not acquire an invented library-upgrade guarantee. D-12 derives publication order from actual manifests, sc-storage first, rehearses exact archives, then proves actual upstream beads-cache PR open/CI green against registry crates. Its independent preparation does not upload until d-11 sanity is closed and completed composition merged, with ratification and actual safety rules passing. Missing release predicates leave publication open.

The phase is one append-only stack with one writer. Metadata layer is planned presentation order; actual link order follows completion. pr_target is the consumed lower bound, not false sibling serialization. Canonical root Cargo.lock is d-12-owned. Historical probe facts remain in Git/review evidence, not a second live scope document.


## Boundary map and generated targets
Read existing boundaries/<crate>/<crate>.toml. sc-config dependencies serde/serde_json unchanged; sc-transport tokio/reqwest/serde->sc-runtime unchanged; sc-command gains sc-storage, consumers sc-cron/sc-cron-commands/sc-runtime; sc-runtime composes transport/command, no storage trait placement there; sc-cron loses direct SQLite backend, depends on sc-storage/sc-command; sc-cron-commands adapts scheduler. Generic writer dependencies sc-storage/rusqlite/Tokio only, NEVER sc-cron/ATM/sc-compose; no consumer SQL/schema. New boundaries/sc-storage/sc-storage.toml has no sc-* dependency. Generated store/service boundaries are emitted by template/boundaries/render.py at boundaries/<prefixed-package>/<prefixed-package>.toml with existing Store/Stores facades; no invented static template boundaries. Application row descriptors/migrations are supplied at open, engine applies them before exposing store.
dependencies.acceptance_criteria:
1. d-11 closes actual generated SQLite app/cron shared database/channel writer, real typed transforms/CRUD and all selected engines/mixed layouts; no vulnerable SQLx SQLite or separate cron.db default, no fake engine proof.
2. d-12 closes actual upstream migration PR open/CI-green at exact SHA against eight published0.3.0 crates; no path/patch/Git SDK substitute. All source/package/API/docs and normal test suites pass.
3. Generic backends contain no consumer table code; named owned retryable atomic API and static+runtime safety checks actually operate. Public changed storage APIs return typed errors/no panic; writer panic fails every waiting caller. External rule and ratification blockers stay explicit until met.
4. All existing workspace/lint/test/boundary/publishing-kit/controlled-host benchmark gates pass; publication waits for closed d-11 sanity and owner ratification, after exact archive rehearsal. Required coverage and independent plan/development gates are separate from schema validation.
